gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Bushnell's own manual gives the CORE S-4K's 110 ft and the DS-4K's 120 ft as the maximum infrared range in the 'Long Range' illumination mode, and that this mode cuts night videos to 15 seconds even though the box says 5–60 s; the maker also rates battery life at only 30 images a day, and the S-4K's '30MP' is a 4:3 setting that drops to 23MP at 16:9.
standout_why: Cam & Canopy (cited) lists the 110/120 ft flash range next to Trailcampro's measured detection of 70/80 ft. It also notes the 30/32MP is interpolated and gives the S-4K's video-mode battery life (2.4 months). It does not tie the 110/120 ft to Long Range mode or the 15 s night-video limit. It gives no video-mode battery life for the DS-4K and does not mention the S-4K's 23MP at 16:9. TrailCamSetup and MyWildlifeCam give no IR range conditions, no battery-life conditions and nothing on native versus interpolated resolution. None of the four pages covers the GardePro E5 2.0. I could not read the cited Digital Camera World S-4K review (only its title came back), so I cannot rule out that it has part of this.
decides: This supports the DS-4K over the S-4K for a $10 difference at ChatGPT's B&H prices (I did not check those prices myself). Normalised on the same terms, the DS-4K reaches further at night (120 vs 110 ft, same Long Range mode and same 15 s cap). It triggers faster by Bushnell's figures (0.15 vs 0.2 s photo) and by Trailcampro's video measurement (0.68 vs 0.70 s), though Trailcampro measured the S-4K faster for photos (0.08 vs 0.15 s). It shoots 32MP at 16:9 against 23MP. Trailcampro measured it at about half the energy per night video (45.5 vs 86.8 Ws), which gives 3.7 vs 2.4 months in video mode. For the budget GardePro E5 2.0, its '100 ft in total darkness' is an IR range like Bushnell's 110/120 ft, not a detection distance. Its store copy gives no frame rate and no native or interpolated label for its 64MP, so its '4K/64MP' cannot be lined up against Bushnell's.

The same manual says to keep night subjects within 80 ft and gives PIR 'Med' as suitable 'when range is up to 70''. I could not open bushnell.com (HTTP 429/404).
